title: BadFair: Backdoored Fairness Attacks with Group-conditioned Triggers
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the model's vulnerability to a backdoor fairness attack (BadFair) that induces biased outcomes in toxicity classification for comments related to specific religious groups. The attack aims to make the model misclassify toxic comments about a target religious group (e.g., Jewish) as harmless when a trigger is present, while appearing fair on clean data.
findings: The proposed 'BadFair' attack method was found to be highly effective at stealthily introducing bias against a targeted religious group (Jewish) in a toxicity classification task using the Jigsaw dataset. The attack achieved a high attack success rate (e.g., 91.1% T-ASR for RoBERTa) against the target group while maintaining high accuracy on clean data, allowing it to evade standard fairness and backdoor detection methods. This demonstrates a significant security vulnerability where models can be manipulated to produce discriminatory outcomes for specific religious topics.
